title: Simultaneous strict Roos, counit and quotient augmentation normalization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L\subset M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, allowing equality, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizers $\varpi_F$, and $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes considered have $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On fixed small skeletons of their pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], put $R_{F,W}=\lim_n(A_{F,n})_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathscr S_F(W)$ for strict quotient-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, $\mathcal R_{F,W}$ for derived reduction, and $\mathcal L_{F,W}=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for realization, with their specified whole-system adjunction $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$ and actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

For a strict tower complex $D$ of $R_{F,W}$-modules with transitions $t_n$, put $H(D)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_D)[-1]$, where $s_D((a_n)_n)=(t_na_{n+1})_n$, using termwise products. The single functor $H$ on all such towers admits a natural isomorphism $\rho_D:H(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim D$ with the following simultaneous normalization. For a K-injective tower resolution $q:D\to I$ with injective terms [def-pur-kinjective-complex], the ordinary limit inclusion $j_I:\lim I\to H(I)$, with limit tuple in the unshifted product and zero in the shifted product, is a quasi-isomorphism and $\rho_D=[j_I]^{-1}[H(q)]$ under $R\lim D=\lim I$. This comparison is independent of the resolution and commutes with each derived projection.

For any $C\in D(\mathscr S_F(W))$ put $D=\operatorname{Res}C$. The whole-system counit $e_C:\mathcal R\mathcal LC\to C$ evaluates to the derived-change-of-rings adjunct [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] of the $n$th component of the single tower map
$$\epsilon_D:\Delta R\lim D\longrightarrow D,\qquad \epsilon_D=[q]^{-1}\circ[\Delta\lim I\longrightarrow I].$$
The component is $[q_n]^{-1}$ composed with the ordinary $n$th limit projection. In particular this formula computes the fixed counit, retaining all quotient transitions, rather than selecting independent levelwise lifts.

For any ambient $K\in D(R_{F,W})$ and flat-term K-flat representative $p:P\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], let $P_n=P\otimes_{R_{F,W}}(A_{F,n})_W$, with actual quotient transitions. Writing the shifted coordinate first, the augmentation
$$v_P:P\longrightarrow H(\operatorname{Res}(P_n)_n),\qquad z\longmapsto(0,(z\otimes1)_n)$$
is a chain map and satisfies the equality of entire derived morphisms
$$u_K=\rho_{\operatorname{Res}(P_n)_n}[v_P][p]^{-1}.$$
Here $(1-s)(z\otimes1)_n=0$ because the actual quotient maps preserve $z\otimes1$. The counit and augmentation formulas are natural and independent of all K-injective and K-flat resolutions. No completeness, constructibility or boundedness of $K$ or $C$ is imposed.

proof.text: Let η be the canonical rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ of ordinary inverse limit. A quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], which additive inverse limit preserves. Thus the K-injective localizer derives inverse limit; η is invertible on K-injectives by rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_eq. The derived universal property gives the required bijection on natural transformations. Apply [lem-coef-derived-tower-counit-projections] to η and the fixed inverse-limit functor, with K-injective resolutions from the coefficient tower category. This supplies an adjunction and its whole-tower counit equation. The equality D.limitUnit_I = Q(D.towerLimitComparison.inv_I) followed by η_I and naturality of the constant functor localization factorization transform that equation to the displayed one with D.limitUnit.

proof.text: For every quasi-isomorphism q:X→I with I K-injective, define j=asIso(Q(roosι I)), and d=asIso(D.limitUnit_I) followed by the derived-limit image of asIso(Qq) inverse. The equation d Rlim(Qq)=D.limitUnit_I follows by cancellation. Cancel Rlim(Qq) and use naturality of D.roos and its inclusion normalization to obtain the Roos resolution formula. Naturality of the fixed projection and evaluation comparison, with the calculation in step 3, gives the resolution projection formula. Compose the counit equation with Qq and use counit naturality and the preceding equality for d; cancel Qq to obtain the entire counit formula at X. All formulas hold for every resolution and use the same natural maps, so are independent of resolution choices.

retained_arguments.text: For each scheme $W$ and coefficient field $F$, form the same strict-tower cone functor $H(D)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_D)[-1]$ on restricted quotient-system complexes. Countable products of $R_{F,W}$-modules are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] supplies a natural isomorphism $\rho_D:H(D)\simeq R\lim D$ on the entire derived tower category. Use this functor and this comparison throughout. Its specified inclusion of an ordinary limit into the cone is the limit tuple in the unshifted product and zero in the shifted product. Its comparison with a K-injective tower model is independent of the resolution. This constructs the Roos part of the requested interface, including its normalization, before choosing any pullback or scalar representatives.

retained_arguments.text:
Use the specified derived adjunction $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], rather than selecting maps independently at its levels. For a restricted tower $D=\operatorname{Res}C$ and a K-injective resolution $q:D\to I$, compute $R\lim D$ by $\lim I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its limit projections are represented, simultaneously as a map of towers, by
$$\Delta\lim I\longrightarrow I\xrightarrow{[q]^{-1}}D.$$
Indeed the first map is the ordinary limit cone; composing its $n$th projection with $[q_n]^{-1}$ is precisely the total-limit projection to $D_n$. The evaluation of $e_C$ is its scalar-extension adjunct by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. This gives the formula in the statement for $\epsilon_D$, with the indicated order of composition. The whole-system counit, including its quotient transitions, already exists in that adjunction; the calculation identifies its evaluated adjuncts and does not attempt to construct a system map from a collection of unrelated derived maps.

retained_arguments.text:
For the initial completion map use the actual adjunction unit, not an arbitrary map having its levelwise projections. On $P\to K$ the strict quotient augmentation is
$$v_P:P\longrightarrow H(\operatorname{Res}\mathcal RP),\qquad z\longmapsto(0,(z\otimes1)_n),$$
where the shifted product is written first. It is a chain map because each quotient transition sends $z\otimes1$ to $z\otimes1$, so $(1-s)(z\otimes1)_n=0$. The whole-morphism equality $u_K=\rho[v_P][P\to K]^{-1}$, including its resolution-independent interpretation, is exactly [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model]. This gives the zero shifted coordinate required by [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models].
